data.description:
## Context / Problem

Over the MCP server, `claim_ticket` (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:300-318`) calls `rebar.claim`, whose claim event stamps `("session", resolve_session_id())` and `("harness", resolve_harness())` from the **server process's** environment (`src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:71-72`, resolver at `src/rebar/_commands/session_id.py:63`). On the AWS deployment those variables describe the server, not the calling agent, so every MCP-driven claim records no usable `claimed_session`, and `cross_session_warning_for` (`src/rebar/_commands/cross_session.py:45`) is silent for every MCP caller. The inbox feed (the dependent child) needs a recipient identity that exists on the mandated MCP path.

## Approach

Resolve an **MCP acting-session identity** on the server as `principal` + optional `session_hint`, scoped so a client can never select another principal's identity:

- `principal` = the authenticated client identity the auth composite already yields (`claims.get("sub")` at `src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py:334`, one PAT per harness per `docs/mcp-client-setup.md:25-27`), or the proxy-forwarded identity already held in the `PROXY_IDENTITY` ContextVar (`src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py:63`) when that path is active.
- `session_hint` = the value of a new request header `X-Rebar-Session-Id`, read by the same header-guard middleware pattern that reads the proxy identity header (`src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py:90-135`), stored in a new request-scoped ContextVar `MCP_SESSION_HINT` in the same module. Length-capped (128 chars) and restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`; anything else is treated as absent. The MCP transport `Mcp-Session-Id` is deliberately **not** used as a fallback (it churns on reconnect and blue-green cutover, bug `aca0-6a66-0a27-47cf`).
- `resolve_session_id()` gains one higher-precedence source ahead of `REBAR_SESSION_ID`: when the MCP request context holds a principal, return `mcp:<principal>` or `mcp:<principal>/<session_hint>` when the hint is present; `resolve_harness()` returns `mcp:<principal>` in that case. Outside an MCP request the ContextVars are unset and behavior is byte-identical to today.
- Because the composite value is what `_fold_claimed_session` (`src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py:25`) stores, `cross_session_warning` starts working over MCP with no reducer change: the pure detector compares strings.
- Client-config recipes in `docs/mcp-client-setup.md`: Claude Code `.mcp.json`/user config `headers: {"X-Rebar-Session-Id": "${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID}"}` (the existing `Authorization: Bearer ${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLAUDE}` header already relies on that expansion); Codex `env_http_headers`; Cursor `${env:VAR}`; OpenCode `{env:VAR}`. The documented degradation when the hint is absent: all sessions of one principal share one identity (`mcp:<principal>`).

Positive rationale: this reuses the exact seam and trust discipline the auth middleware already has for a forwarded identity header, adds no new auth path, and keeps the store schema untouched (`claimed_session`/`claim_harness` are existing nullable strings). Riskiest assumption, tested first: that Claude Code expands `${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID}` in an HTTP header at connect time (open bugs anthropics/claude-code#6204, #51581 concern header substitution). Step 1 is a throwaway probe: point a local Claude Code session at the deployed server with the header configured and read the received hint back through a temporary debug log line; the probe's verdict is recorded on this ticket and decides whether the Claude Code recipe ships as "supported" or "principal-only until the harness fixes expansion". No repository artifact is left by the probe.

Failure disposition: a malformed or over-long hint is dropped (identity degrades to `mcp:<principal>`), never an error — the header is advisory sub-partitioning, not authentication.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py` — `MCP_SESSION_HINT` ContextVar; header extraction and validation in the existing header-guard middleware; `current_mcp_identity()` helper returning `(principal, hint)`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/session_id.py` — MCP-request source ahead of the env-var list in `resolve_session_id()` / `resolve_harness()`.
- `src/rebar/mcp_server.py` — wire the middleware for the new header on the same app the auth guard wraps.
- `docs/mcp-client-setup.md`, `docs/mcp-auth.md` (header semantics, trust scope), `docs/session-id-shims.md` (correct the stale "`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is remote-only" note — the local CLI exports it in 2.1.x), `docs/event-schema.md` (the `mcp:<principal>[/<hint>]` value shape of `claimed_session`).
- `tests/unit/test_session_id.py`, `tests/unit/test_mcp_auth.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_claim_session.py` (new).

## Testing

- Unit (pure): `resolve_session_id()` precedence matrix — MCP context set with/without hint, malformed hint, no MCP context → env chain unchanged (negative control: existing tests stay green byte-for-byte).
- Unit (middleware): header present/absent/over-long/bad-charset → ContextVar value; a header on a request that fails auth never reaches the ContextVar.
- Contract (MCP in-process client, the tier that crosses auth + tool + reducer): `claim_ticket` with the header → `show_ticket` reports `claimed_session == "mcp:<principal>/<hint>"` and `claim_harness == "mcp:<principal>"`; a second in-process client under the same principal with a different hint calling `comment_ticket` receives a non-null `cross_session_warning`; the same hint → null (contrast case).
- Gate: all under `make test`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `claim_ticket` over the MCP server records `claimed_session` as `mcp:<principal>/<hint>` when `X-Rebar-Session-Id` is sent and `mcp:<principal>` when it is not; verified by `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_claim_session.py`.
- [ ] `comment_ticket` over MCP from a different session hint under the same principal returns a non-null `cross_session_warning`, and the same hint returns null; verified by the contrast test in the same file.
- [ ] A hint longer than 128 chars or outside `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]` is ignored and the claim still succeeds with `mcp:<principal>`; verified by `tests/unit/test_mcp_auth.py`.
- [ ] Outside an MCP request, `resolve_session_id()` output is unchanged for every existing env-var case; verified by the existing `tests/unit/test_session_id.py` cases passing unmodified plus one new no-context case.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The header-expansion probe verdict for Claude Code (expands / does not expand, with the harness version and timestamp) is recorded as a comment on this ticket before the client recipe is marked supported in `docs/mcp-client-setup.md`.
- [ ] `docs/session-id-shims.md` no longer states that `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is exposed only in the remote runner; verified by grep in the docs-drift gate.
data.title: MCP session identity: principal + X-Rebar-Session-Id hint, claimed_session stamped and cross_session_warning live over MCP
